overview: This resolution, passed by both the House and Senate, allows Emancipation Hall in the U.S. Capitol Visitor Center to be used on December 16, 2025, for a ceremony unveiling a statue of Barbara Rose Johns. Johns was a Virginia student who in 1951 led a walkout to protest conditions at her segregated high school, a protest that fed into the legal fight against school segregation. The Architect of the Capitol, the office that manages the Capitol buildings and grounds, sets the conditions for preparing the space. It does not change any law. Congress gave it final approval on December 4, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution allows a fitting public ceremony to honor a young civil rights figure from Virginia.
against: Critics say there is little to object to; the resolution only approves the use of a room for an event and does not change any law or spending.
